## Data Munging


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
weirddad_clean <- weirddad %>%
  dplyr::select(college, is_dad_weird) %>%
  tidyr::drop_na(c(college, is_dad_weird)) %>%
  mutate(
    college = factor(college),
    is_dad_weird = factor(is_dad_weird, levels = c("Yes", "No"))
  )
```

  gf_bar(~college, fill = ~is_dad_weird, position = "fill") %>%

### Inference

-   more SMI students think their dad is weird than MIT students.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
weirddad %>%
  drop_na() %>%
  gf_bar(~is_dad_weird, fill = ~gender, position = "fill") %>%
  gf_labs(
    x = "Is your dad weird?",
    title = "Proportion of Students saying their dad is weird - Gender wise"
  )
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](weirddad_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-10-1.png){width=672}
:::
:::


### Inference

-   Gender does not appear to influence whether students think their dad is weird.

-   Males and females show almost equal proportions saying “Yes” or “No.”

-   This pattern shows the idea that perception of dad weirdness is gender-neutral — both male and female students perceive their fathers similarly.

## Chi Sqaure Test


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
contingency_table <- vcd::structable(college ~ is_dad_weird,
  data = weirddad_clean
)
contingency_table
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
             college MIT SMI
is_dad_weird                
Yes                    5  12
No                    28  19
```


:::
:::


At MIT, 5 out of 33 students (15%) said their dad is weird. At SMI, 12 out of 31 students (39%) said their dad is weird.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
gss_vcd_table <- vcd::structable(is_dad_weird ~ college, data = weirddad_clean)
gss_vcd_table %>%
  vcd::mosaic(
    gp = shading_hsv, direction = "v",
    main = "College vs 'Is Dad Weird?' Mosaic Chart",
    legend = TRUE
      )
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](weirddad_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-12-1.png){width=672}
:::
:::



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
contingency_table <- vcd::structable(college ~ is_dad_weird, data = weirddad_clean)
contingency_table <- as.table(contingency_table)
xq_test_object <- xchisq.test(contingency_table)
```

```

xq_test_object %>%

X_squared_observed
```

```

```

::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
# Determine the Chi-Square critical value
X_squared_critical <- qchisq(
  p = .05,
  df = (5 - 1) * (2 - 1), # (nrows-1) * (ncols-1)
  lower.tail = FALSE
)
X_squared_critical
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
[1] 9.487729
```


:::
:::



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
test_result <- chisq.test(contingency_table)

# Extract required values
X_squared_observed <- test_result$statistic
df <- test_result$parameter
X_squared_critical <- qchisq(0.95, df)
```
:::



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
mosaic::xqchisq(
  p = 0.95, df = df,
  return = c("plot"), verbose = F,
  system = "gg"
) %>%
  gf_labs(
    x = "Chi-Square Value", title = "Critical and Observed Chi-Square Values",
    x = ""
  ) %>%
  gf_vline(
    xintercept = X_squared_observed,
    color = "red", linewidth = 1
  ) %>%
  gf_vline(
    xintercept = X_squared_critical,
    color = "dodgerblue", linewidth = 1
  ) %>%
  gf_annotate(
    x = X_squared_observed - 1, y = 0.15,
    geom = "label", label = "Observed\nChi-Square",
    fill = "red", alpha = 0.3
  ) %>%
  gf_annotate("curve", X_squared_observed - 1,
    y = 0.135, yend = 0.10,
    xend = X_squared_observed - 0.3,
    linewidth = 0.5, curvature = 0.3,
    arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.25, "cm"))
  ) %>%
  gf_annotate(
    x = X_squared_critical + 1, y = 0.15,
    geom = "label", label = "Critical\nChi-Square",
    fill = "lightblue"
  ) %>%
  gf_annotate("curve", X_squared_critical + 1,
    y = 0.135, yend = 0.10,
    xend = X_squared_critical + 0.3,
    linewidth = 0.5, curvature = -0.3,
    arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.25, "cm"))
  ) %>%
  gf_refine(
    scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(add = c(0, 0.01))),
    scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(add = c(0, 1)))
  )
```

## Propotion Test


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}

  group_by(is_dad_weird) %>%
  count()
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
# A tibble: 2 × 2
# Groups:   is_dad_weird [2]
  is_dad_weird     n
  <fct>        <int>
1 Yes             17
2 No              47
```


:::
:::



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
glimpse(weirddad_clean)
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
Rows: 64
Columns: 2
$ college      <fct> SMI, SMI, SMI, SMI, MIT, MIT, MIT, SMI, SMI, SMI, SMI, SM…
$ is_dad_weird <fct> No, No, No, Yes, No, No, No, No, Yes, Yes, Yes, Yes, No, …
```


:::
:::



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
weirddad_clean %>%
  summarize(prop = mean(is_dad_weird == "Yes"), n = n())
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
      prop  n
1 0.265625 64
```


:::
:::


### Inference

-   The difference in the proportion of students saying “Yes, my dad is weird” in college is statistically significant.

-   Across both colleges (MIT and SMI combined), about 26.6% of students said their dad is weird.

-   This means that most students (≈73%) do not consider their dad weird, suggesting that “weird dads” are a minority perception overall.

-   MIT: 15% “weird dads” SMI: 39% “weird dads”

-   That contrast shows that SMI is well above the overall average (26.6%), while MIT is below it.

-   SMI dads are perceived as significantly weirder than MIT dads.


::: {.cell}
